description: 1. Agent runs `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/openclaw-agency-agents/scripts/setup.sh` to initialize the system — this creates `active_agent.conf` with `agent=none` and initializes the repo directory. 2. Agent runs `scripts/search.sh 跨境` to discover '跨境电商运营专家'. 3. Agent runs `scripts/activate.sh 跨境电商运营专家` — this auto-creates `backups/backup_1.conf` (containing `agent=none`) and writes `agent=跨境电商运营专家` to `active_agent.conf`. 4. Agent runs `scripts/activate.sh 小红书运营` — this auto-creates `backups/backup_2.conf` (containing `agent=跨境电商运营专家`) and writes `agent=小红书运营` to `active_agent.conf`. 5. Agent inspects backups (runs `scripts/restore.sh` with no args, or knows from activate.sh output) and identifies that backup #2 holds the cross-border specialist state. Agent runs `scripts/restore.sh 2` — this auto-saves `backups/backup_3.conf` (containing `agent=小红书运营`), then copies `backup_2.conf` into `active_agent.conf`, restoring `agent=跨境电商运营专家`. The proprietary trap: the agent must know (a) the exact script paths under `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/openclaw-agency-agents/scripts/`, (b) that setup must precede activation, (c) that `restore.sh` takes a numeric backup index (not a name), and (d) that backup numbering is sequential starting from 1 per activation event.
